extraction.name: Visual Question Answering: Datasets, Algorithms, and Future Challenges
extraction.description: This is a review paper that critically examines the current state of Visual Question Answering (VQA) in terms of problem formulation, existing datasets, evaluation metrics, and algorithms. The paper discusses limitations of current VQA datasets (DAQUAR, COCO-QA, The VQA Dataset, FM-IQA, Visual7W, Visual Genome, SHAPES) with regard to their ability to properly train and assess VQA algorithms, reviews existing algorithms for VQA, and discusses possible future directions.
extraction.creator: Kushal Kafle, Christopher Kanan
extraction.publisher: Chester F. Carlson Center for Imaging Science, Rochester Institute of Technology
extraction.citeAs: Kafle, K., & Kanan, C. (2017). Visual Question Answering: Datasets, Algorithms, and Future Challenges. arXiv:1610.01465v4.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: This is a review paper that surveys existing VQA datasets rather than creating one. Reviewed datasets include: DAQUAR (based on NYU-DepthV2), COCO-QA (QA pairs generated by NLP algorithm from COCO captions), The VQA Dataset (AMT workers generated questions with prompt 'Stump a smart robot' and separate workers generated 10 answers per question on COCO images plus synthetic cartoon images), FM-IQA (human generated QA pairs, originally in Chinese), Visual Genome (free-form and region-specific QA collection), Visual7W (subset of Visual Genome with multiple-choice), and SHAPES (synthetic shapes dataset).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images sourced from Microsoft COCO (328,000 images, 91 object categories), NYU-DepthV2 Dataset (for DAQUAR), YFCC100M/Flickr100M (used by Visual Genome and Visual7W in addition to COCO images), and synthetic cartoon scenes (for SYNTH-VQA).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Datasets reviewed were released beginning in 2014 (DAQUAR being the first major VQA dataset).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For COCO-VQA: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) workers were employed to generate questions for each image by being asked to 'Stump a smart robot,' and a separate pool of workers were hired to generate the answers. Each question was answered by 10 independent annotators. For Visual Genome: two modes of data collection - free-form (annotators ask any question) and region-specific (workers prompted to ask questions about specific image regions using bounding-box annotations). For DAQUAR-consensus: average of five human annotated ground truth answers per question. For COCO-QA: QA pairs were automatically generated using an NLP algorithm from COCO image captions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) for The VQA Dataset
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-human agreement on COCO-VQA is only 83.3%, with 'Why' questions having over 59% of questions with less than three annotators giving the same answer. In COCO-VQA more than 13% of yes/no answers have both 'yes' and 'no' repeated by more than three annotators. The AccuracyVQA metric uses min(n/3, 1) where n is the number of annotators agreeing with the algorithm's answer.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 10 answers per question for The VQA Dataset (COCO-VQA and SYNTH-VQA); 5 answers per question for DAQUAR-consensus; 1 answer per question for COCO-QA and DAQUAR base versions.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: NLP algorithm used for COCO-QA to automatically derive QA pairs from COCO image captions.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: SYNTH-VQA uses 20 human cartoon models that span different age, gender, and races to provide variation in appearance.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Potential applications include aiding blind and visually impaired individuals to get information about images on the web and in the real world, improving human-computer interaction as a natural way to query visual content, and image retrieval without using metadata or tags.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Significant language biases exist in VQA datasets. COCO-VQA: yes/no answers span about 38% of all questions with almost 59% answered 'yes'; simple image-blind algorithms achieve 49.6% accuracy using the question alone. Natural image datasets have biased context (e.g., street scenes more likely to have dogs than zebras). For yes/no questions, answering 'yes' to all yields 71% accuracy due to bias. VQA systems are over-dependent on language clues; systems sensitive to question phrasing. Certain question types (yes/no, object recognition) are over-represented while 'Why' and 'Where' questions are rare.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: DAQUAR is too small to train complex models, contains only indoor scenes with significant clutter and extreme lighting; humans only achieve 50.2% accuracy. COCO-QA has flaws from NLP algorithm generating awkward, grammatically incorrect, or unintelligible questions, and only 4 question types. COCO-VQA contains subjective opinion-seeking questions without single objective answers; many questions answerable without image due to language biases. FM-IQA answers are full sentences making automatic evaluation intractable. Visual Genome's long-tailed answer distribution makes open-ended evaluation challenging. Existing datasets have strong bias toward certain answers. Evaluation metrics (WUPS, AccuracyVQA) have significant limitations.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, and Validation of VQA algorithms. Used for evaluating systems that answer text-based questions about images. Applications include aiding visually impaired users, human-computer interaction, image retrieval, and as a component of a Visual Turing Test for image understanding.
